passages.note: Bill details page names the author (Glick) and the Governor's signature, not Garten's own act.

passages.provision_quote: a criminal act, except when performed under the following circumstances:
passages.note: Operative ban clause of SB 1(ss), the instrument Garten voted on.

passages.provision_quote: for reasons based upon the professional, medical judgment of the pregnant woman's physician, if either: (i) the abortion is necessary when reasonable medical judgment dictates that performing the abortion is necessary to prevent any serious health risk to the pregnant woman or to save the pregnant woman's life; or (ii) the fetus is diagnosed with a lethal fetal anomaly;
passages.note: States the exception for a serious health risk to, or to save the life of, the mother, and for a lethal fetal anomaly.

passages.provision_quote: if: (A) the pregnancy is a result of rape or incest;
passages.note: States the exception for pregnancies resulting from rape or incest.
Senate concurrence roll call shows Garten's Yea vote on SB 1(ss).

rows.reasoning: Garten's Yea vote on the Senate concurrence roll call (Aug. 5, 2022) shows his own act on SB 1(ss) (2022 First Special Session), a single-subject abortion bill that makes abortion 'a criminal act, except when performed under the following circumstances,' permitting it only for a serious health risk to or to save the life of the mother, a lethal fetal anomaly, or (within the first ten weeks) rape or incest. These operative clauses match rung 4, 'ban abortion except in cases of rape, incest, or a serious risk to the mother's life.'
